title: fix(ingestion): scope extractor timeout to single LLM call
description:
## Summary
The Extractor wrapped its whole invoke (all chunks, all phases) in one fixed 600s budget, so any large-but-healthy document (e.g. 3000 chunks) inevitably failed with `context deadline exceeded` and lost the entire parse.

This PR moves the timeout to a per-LLM-call budget (default 180s, `EXTRACTOR_CHAT_TIMEOUT` override). The budget is a hung-call ceiling, not pacing, so per-model speed variance needs no tuning. A call that exceeds it skips its chunk instead of failing the document.

## Related Issue
None.

## Changes
- `internal/ingestion/component/extractor.go`
  - Remove the node-level `runtime.WithTimeout(600s)` in `Invoke`; phases run on the parent ctx (task cancellation still aborts).
  - Add per-call budget in `callRaw` around `inv.Chat` (`extractorChatTimeout()`, env `EXTRACTOR_CHAT_TIMEOUT` seconds, default 180s).
  - Pool jobs map a call-budget expiry to a per-chunk skip with warn (`resolveChunkCallError`); non-timeout errors keep fail-fast; parent cancel propagates.
  - All-chunks-timed-out in a phase fails loudly (`checkAllChunksSkipped`) so a down model cannot silently produce empty extractions.
- `internal/ingestion/component/extractor_call_timeout_test.go` (new): slow-chunk skip, all-hang failure, parent-cancel propagation, env parsing.

## Test Plan
- `bash build.sh --test ./internal/ingestion/component/` passes (includes 4 new tests, ~1s each for timeout cases).
- `gofmt` clean.

bugs.summary: extractorChatTimeout accepts any positive integer from EXTRACTOR_CHAT_TIMEOUT and multiplies it by time.Second without a range check, so a value above math.MaxInt64/1e9 seconds overflows into a negative duration instead of falling back to the 180-second default; every Extractor LLM call then times out immediately.
bugs.trigger: EXTRACTOR_CHAT_TIMEOUT=9223372037 (one more than the largest representable number of seconds): extractorChatTimeout returns about -2562047h instead of 3m0s.
